Fix a field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, an integer $d\ge2$, and positive integers $n_1,\ldots,n_d$. A finite order-$d$ tensor of shape $(n_1,\ldots,n_d)$ is an array $A=(A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d})$ indexed by $1\le i_k\le n_k$. Its Frobenius inner product and norm are
$$ \langle A,B\rangle_F=\sum_{i_1=1}^{n_1}\cdots\sum_{i_d=1}^{n_d}\overline{A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}}B_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}, \qquad \|A\|_F=\sqrt{\langle A,A\rangle_F}. $$
For a matrix, rank means the dimension of its column image and the Frobenius inner product is the same entrywise formula. The adjoint $M^*$ is conjugate transpose (transpose over $\mathbb R$).

For $1\le k\le d$, the mode-$k$ unfolding $A_{(k)}$ has $n_k$ rows and $\prod_{j\ne k}n_j$ columns. Its row index is $i_k$ and its column index is the remaining tuple in increasing mode order, lexicographically ordered. Its entry at that row and column is the corresponding entry of $A$. For $1\le k<d$, the cut-$k$ unfolding $A^{\langle k\rangle}$ has row tuple $(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and column tuple $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$, each lexicographically ordered. Let $d\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set, and
let $1<p<\infty$ satisfy $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. Put
$V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and
$p'=p/(p-1)$. The Poincaré inequality makes this norm equivalent to the full
$W^{1,p}$ norm. [[lem-pe12-w0p-separable-reflexive]] gives separability and
reflexivity, while [[lem-pe12-w1p-compact-l2-embedding]] gives the dense
continuous compact inclusion $V\Subset H$; these are the hypotheses of the
evolution triple in [[def-pe12-gelfand-triple]]. The compact-inclusion result
uses the stated threshold also when $d=1$, where it reduces to $p>1$.

A measurable flux $a:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is an admissible
**coercive monotone diffusion flux of p-growth** if it is Carathéodory (for
each $\xi$, $x\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is measurable, and for almost every $x$,
$\xi\mapsto a(x,\xi)$ is continuous), and there are constants $C<\infty$,
$\alpha>0$, nonnegative functions $g\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ and
$h\in L^1(\Omega)$, and one
null set outside which, for all $\xi,\eta\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|a(x,\xi)|\le C\bigl(g(x)+|\xi|^{p-1}\bigr),\qquad a(x,\xi)\cdot\xi\ge\alpha|\xi|^p-h(x),$$
$$\bigl(a(x,\xi)-a(x,\eta)\bigr)\cdot(\xi-\eta)\ge0.$$
The induced operator $A:V\to V^*$ is
$$\langle A(v),w\rangle_{V^*,V} =\int_\Omega a(x,\nabla v(x))\cdot\nabla w(x)\,dx.$$
The growth bound and Hölder's inequality make this pairing finite and give
$\|A(v)\|_{V^*}\le C_1(\|g\|_{p'}+\|v\|_V^{p-1})$ for a constant $C_1$.
The finite-dimensional test-coordinate continuity used in the backward Euler
existence argument follows from the stated Carathéodory and growth conditions
by dominated convergence, as proved in
[[thm-pe12-backward-euler-galerkin-existence-energy]]. No additional global
operator-continuity hypothesis is imposed.

For $f\in L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, a weak evolution solution is a function
$u\in W_p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ with a continuous $H$ representative
such that $u'+A(u)=f$ in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$ and $u(0)=u_0\in H$.

For every $w\in H^1(K)$, $w\circ F_K\in H^1(\widehat K)$ by [F8], and the weak Green functional, affine weak-derivative/divergence transformations, and change of variables give $$\langle\gamma_{n,K}\tau,[w]\rangle=\int_{\widehat K}\bigl(\widehat\tau\cdot\widehat\nabla(w\circ F_K)+(\widehat{\operatorname{div}}\widehat\tau)(w\circ F_K)\bigr) =\langle\gamma_{\widehat n,\widehat K}\widehat\tau,[w\circ F_K]\rangle.$$ The volume moments also transport: for $p\in P_1(K)^2$, affine change of variables gives $$(\Pi^{div}_3\tau,p)_K=(\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau,A_K^{\mathsf T}(p\circ F_K))_{\widehat K},\qquad A_K^{\mathsf T}(p\circ F_K)\in P_1(\widehat K)^2,$$ and the same identity with $\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau$ replaced by $\widehat\tau$; hence every physical $P_1(K)^2$ volume moment is matched. Since this holds for every such $\psi$, the two outward weak normal traces cancel as distributions on the relative interior of each interior facet. Assume Countable Choice for the published Sobolev interfaces cited below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and use real scalars. $L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ means the $d$-tuple of real $L^2$ equivalence classes, with norm $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^d\|v_j\|_2^2$. The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$
and equip it with the graph norm
$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
The Sobolev notation $H^1(D)=W^{1,2}(D)$ and $H^1_0(D)=W^{1,2}_0(D)$ uses the norm and zero-boundary closure conventions of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]. No pointwise boundary value is part of this definition.

By [F4], $I_h^1u\to u$ in $H(\operatorname{curl})$ as $h\to0$, and [F9] gives $u\in H_0(\operatorname{curl})$. Uniform bounds on $E_{tt}$ give $L^2$-Lipschitz continuity of $E_t$ by the pointwise mean-value bound [F8]. For a compact smooth vector test $\psi$, dominated differentiation gives $\frac d{dt}(\operatorname{curl}E_t,\psi)=\frac d{dt}(E_t,\operatorname{curl}\psi)=(E_{tt},\operatorname{curl}\psi)=(\operatorname{curl}E_{tt},\psi)$. The uniform bound on $\operatorname{curl}E_{tt}$ and [F8], followed by $L^2$ density, therefore give $\|\operatorname{curl}E_t(t)-\operatorname{curl}E_t(s)\|_2\le K|t-s|$. The same test identities for $E$ show $E$ is graph-norm $C^1$ with derivative $E_t$: subtract the value of $E_t(s)$ from its difference quotient and use the just-proved Lipschitz bound, first in test pairings and then by density. Difference quotients of $E_t$ are uniformly graph bounded; their $L^2$ parts converge to $E_{tt}$ by dominated convergence, and their curls converge distributionally to $\operatorname{curl}E_{tt}$. Density and uniform boundedness upgrade the latter to weak $L^2$ convergence. Consequently every bounded graph-linear functional of $E_t$ is differentiable with derivative its value on $E_{tt}$. In particular the finite Ritz Gram equations give $(R_hE)_t=R_hE_t$ and $(R_hE)_{tt}=R_hE_{tt}$, with a bounded second derivative; continuity of $E_{tt}$ in the graph norm is unnecessary. [A1, F3, F4, F7, F8, F9, given, algebra]

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Use the preceding mesh-size and boundary-shift lemma. All differential-form notation here is the following finite coefficient notation. A degree-$k$ form in $\mathbb R^3$ is $u=\sum_{I}u_I\,dx^{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{i_k}$, where the sum is over increasing $k$-tuples $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$, the wedge is alternating, and $\|u\|_2^2=\sum_I\|u_I\|_2^2$. The empty wedge is one. Put $du=\sum_I\sum_{j=1}^3(\partial_j u_I)dx^j\wedge dx^I$, with derivatives interpreted distributionally through integration by parts against compactly supported scalar tests; repeated differentials are zero. The graph space $H\Lambda^k$ consists of the coefficient vectors with $u,du\in L^2$, with norm squared $\|u\|_2^2+\|du\|_2^2$; in top degree $d=0$. These formulas agree with the proved smooth coordinate exterior derivative. Identify vector fields with forms by $\sum_{i=1}^3u_i dx_i$ in degree one, $v_1dx_2\wedge dx_3+v_2dx_3\wedge dx_1+v_3dx_1\wedge dx_2$ in degree two, and $q\,dx_1\wedge dx_2\wedge dx_3$ in degree three. Thus expansion of the finite formula for $d$ gives grad, curl, and div with exactly these signs; the degree-two coefficients in increasing order are $(v_3,-v_2,v_1)$, so their Euclidean norm equals that of $v$. For a smooth map $G$ from an open subset of $\mathbb R^q$ to $\mathbb R^3$, define its pullback by the finite tangent-Jacobian-minor formula
$$G^*u=\sum_{J}\left(\sum_I u_I(G)\det\bigl(\partial_{j_b}G^{i_a}\bigr)_{a,b=1}^k\right)\,dt^{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dt^{j_k}.$$
Here $J$ ranges over increasing $k$-tuples in $1,\ldots,q$; in degree zero this is composition. If $a:T_k\to\sigma$ is the oriented affine simplex parametrization, define $\int_\sigma G^*u$ as the integral over $T_k$ of the coefficient of $(G\circ a)^*u$ on its positive top wedge. Orientation reversal changes its sign; in degree zero it is evaluation. For averaged moments of merely $L^2$ coefficients, the joint parameter integral is the definition and the estimates below prove it exists and is representative-independent. No unbounded trace of an $L^2$ form on a fixed lower-dimensional surface is being defined. This is the existing smooth simplex-integration convention, extended only through the displayed integrable averages. Write $E_h^k$ for the four full Whitney spaces and $E_{h,0}^k$ for the subspaces with all boundary $k$-simplex moments zero; $E_{h,0}^3=E_h^3$. Let $H_0\Lambda^k$ be the graph closure of compactly supported smooth $k$-forms; in degrees zero and one these are $H_0^1$ and the defined $H_0(\operatorname{curl})$.

Fix nonnegative $\rho\in C_c^\infty(B_1)$ with integral one. For each oriented mesh $k$-simplex $\sigma$, define
$$m_{\sigma}^{+,k}(u)=\int_{B_1}\rho(y)\int_\sigma(F_{\epsilon,y}^{+})^*u\,dy,\qquad m_{\sigma}^{-,k}(u)=\int_{B_1}\rho(y)\int_\sigma(F_{\epsilon,y}^{-})^*\widetilde u\,dy,$$
where $\widetilde u$ is zero extension and a degree-zero simplex integral is evaluation. Whitney reconstruction from these moments defines $Q_h^{+,k}:L^2\Lambda^k\to E_h^k$ and $Q_h^{-,k}:L^2\Lambda^k\to E_{h,0}^k$. For $0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$,
$$\|Q_h^{\pm,k}u\|_2\le C\epsilon^{-3/2}\|u\|_2,\qquad \|(Q_h^{\pm,k}-I)v_h\|_2\le C\epsilon\|v_h\|_2,$$
where the second bound uses respectively $v_h\in E_h^k$ or $v_h\in E_{h,0}^k$. Constants are independent of $h,\epsilon$. Furthermore $dQ_h^{+,k}=Q_h^{+,k+1}d$ on $H\Lambda^k$ and $dQ_h^{-,k}=Q_h^{-,k+1}d$ on $H_0\Lambda^k$. The relative Whitney spaces equal $E_h^k\cap H_0\Lambda^k$.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh. The four face-normal fluxes are unisolvent on each $RT_0(K)$, and matching face fluxes assemble a global $H(\operatorname{div})$ field. For smooth scalar $f$, smooth vector fields $u,v$, and the canonical interpolants determined by vertex values, oriented edge circulations, oriented face-normal fluxes, and cell integrals, the interpolation maps satisfy cellwise
$$
abla I_h^0f=I_h^1
abla f,\qquad \operatorname{curl}I_h^1u=I_h^2\operatorname{curl}u,\qquad \operatorname{div}I_h^2v=I_h^3\operatorname{div}v.$$
Any assignment of one real oriented value to each global mesh edge determines a unique assembled field in $N_h^1$; any assignment of one real oriented flux to each global mesh face determines a unique assembled field in $N_h^2$. These assemblies belong to $H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ and $H(\operatorname{div};\Omega)$, respectively, with the global spaces and conventions of [[def-na-lowest-order-whitney-de-rham-spaces]]. Applying the local moment identities to polynomial cell restrictions also proves that the global finite-element spaces form the subcomplex $W_h^0\xrightarrow{
abla}N_h^1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{curl}}N_h^2\xrightarrow{\operatorname{div}}N_h^3$. The canonical interpolation identities themselves apply to smooth inputs; they do not extend the canonical edge moments to arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ inputs.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let
$1<p<\infty$, and let $0<T<\infty$. Put $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm
$\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^p}$, and suppose $V$ has a continuous inclusion in
a real Hilbert space $H$. If $u_j$ is bounded in $L^p(0,T;V)$ and its image
in $L^p(0,T;H)$ converges strongly to $u$, then a subsequence converges
weakly in $L^p(0,T;V)$ to some $U$, the image of $U$ equals $u$, and
$\nabla u_j\rightharpoonup\nabla U$ in
$L^p((0,T)\times\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$.

source_excerpts.excerpt: The chart and chordal fractional norms, trace and lift, exterior energy bound, and weak layer-energy spaces are supplied by [[lem-bem-half-order-bessel-slobodeckij-equivalence]], [[lem-bem-surface-fractional-norm-equivalence]], [[lem-bem-lipschitz-trace-and-lifting]], [[lem-bem-exterior-energy-trace-bound]], and [[def-bem-laplace-layer-potentials-and-energy-spaces]]. The single layer has a common trace and interior-minus-exterior conormal jump equal to its density; its weak energy form is bounded and coercive. The double layer is constructed by a finite-energy transmission problem. [[lem-bem-polyhedral-edge-kernel-representation]] proves that its off-surface kernel representation holds for every global $H^{1/2}$ density, including compatible facewise smooth data that take nonzero values at edges. These are Sobolev trace identities; no pointwise half-jump formula is asserted at an edge or vertex. The weak jump and common conormal results, their mapping bounds, and the Calderón operators appear in [[thm-bem-single-layer-transmission-mapping-and-coercivity]], [[def-bem-double-layer-transmission-space]], [[thm-bem-double-layer-transmission-jumps-and-bounds]], [[def-bem-calderon-boundary-operators]], and [[thm-bem-calderon-mapping-and-jump-identities]]. The hypersingular operator is defined weakly, not by an ordinary absolutely convergent boundary integral; [[thm-bem-hypersingular-ellipticity-and-stabilized-formulation]] proves its quotient ellipticity and constant-mode stabilization.

The analytic suppliers include scalar extension across bounded Lipschitz graph boundaries, a weak local-to-global potential argument, and a Fourier construction of a regular decomposition whose regular vector field and scalar potential both lie in $H_0^1$. The full and relative commuting projections are distinct families: the full family acts on the unrestricted complex, while the relative family preserves the zero-boundary complex and supplies the degree-zero gradient identity used in compactness. Canonical edge moments are defined for polynomial fields and smooth inputs; they do not extend to bounded functionals on all of $H(\operatorname{curl})$. On a contractible polyhedron the relative curl kernel is exactly $\nabla H_0^1$, which yields discrete compactness and the curl Poincaré estimate after removing the discrete gradient gauge. For nontrivial topology, the relative harmonic component must also be removed from that estimate.

[F4] The already assumed AC supplies bounded $H^1$ extension on every bounded Lipschitz domain, connected or not, by [[lem-na-lipschitz-scalar-h1-h2-extension]]. After a bounded-support cutoff, approximate identities converge in $L^2$ for the extension and each first derivative, and convolution commutes with those derivatives. Thus ambient smooth restrictions are $H^1$ dense on bounded annuli. This page defines a one-dimensional full-line conservative finite-volume scheme
for a scalar Cauchy problem, its cellwise state and face-flux reconstructions,
and the Godunov flux for Burgers' equation. The main theorem proves that a
strong local $L^1$ limit of locally uniformly bounded reconstructions satisfies
the distributional weak formulation, including the initial boundary term. The
proof uses cell-time test averages, telescoping interface fluxes, local flux
convergence and separate control of the strip near $t=0$. Convergence and local
boundedness are hypotheses: the theorem proves neither compactness nor entropy
admissibility and assumes no CFL condition.

Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$ be the flux of the one-dimensional system in
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]]. On a periodic uniform
mesh of $N\ge2$ cells of width $h>0$, let $U_i\in\mathcal A$ be the cell means
and put $\nu=\Delta t/h\ge0$. At each face $(i+1/2)$ choose explicit speeds
$S_{L,i+1/2}<0<S_{R,i+1/2}$ and evaluate the middle branch of the HLL flux
[[def-hll-two-wave-flux]] on $(U_i,U_{i+1})$. The **first-order HLL update** is
$$U_i^+=U_i-\nu\bigl(\widehat F_{i+1/2}-\widehat F_{i-1/2}\bigr),\qquad i\pmod N.$$
The speeds are supplied data. Neither this definition nor later algebraic
results assert that they enclose the wave speeds of an exact nonlinear Riemann
solution.

For a two-state problem for a flux $f$ on the open state domain $G$ of
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]], choose explicit speeds
$S_L<S_R$. A signal speed means the propagation speed of one wave in the
particular Riemann solution being approximated. If the HLL model is used as an
enclosing approximation to that fan, its admissibility hypothesis is that
every such speed lies in $[S_L,S_R]$; this definition supplies no general
wave-speed bound.
Set $f_L=f(u_L)$ and $f_R=f(u_R)$. The HLL flux is
$$\widehat f_{\rm HLL}=\begin{cases}f_L,&0\le S_L,\\\dfrac{S_Rf_L-S_Lf_R+S_LS_R(u_R-u_L)}{S_R-S_L},&S_L<0<S_R,\\f_R,&S_R\le0.\end{cases}$$
In the middle case the model has three constant regions separated by the two
waves $S_L,S_R$ and one intermediate state. The wave-speed enclosure is a
separate hypothesis whenever an approximation claim uses it.
